Carol has been a flight attendant for 43 years. Her daughter, Dani, has been one for four. 
Carol lives in Phoenix, Dani lives in LA. One job, two different generations, 370 miles between them, and two totally distinct approaches to their travels.

Flight attendants are often the first people to greet travelers at the start of a trip and the last to see them off before they land somewhere that matters. A vacation, a monumental reunion, the start of a new life somewhere new. It’s a job built around other people’s journeys, which makes it easy to forget how much preparation and care go into the 2-5 trips they make a day.

Introducing Train Jazz. We worked with @j.o.sh.ua to develop and design a live experience from Away and Amtrak, turning every active train in the country into a musical note.

Each train’s place along its route becomes a note’s place in song. Long Distance trains hold long bass tones for the hours they spend between stops. Acela darts in and out of the Northeast Corridor as a fast solo line. Tight clusters of trains sustain a chord; the gaps between them are real silence.

Whatever you’re hearing right now has never been heard before, and won’t be heard again.

One Away carry-on, three colors, three @Amtrak regions.
